title: Require unittest completion before isolated module success
body:
A unittest `load_tests` hook can raise `SystemExit(0)` before discovery finishes. The isolated runner previously treated that zero process exit as a pass and printed `PASS all 2 test modules` in the reproduced two-module fixture, although only the healthy module completed.

Require a per-child completion token written only after `unittest.main(..., exit=False)` returns a successful result, together with exit status zero. Preserve the original discovery arguments seen through `sys.argv`, ordered captured output, independent interpreters, concurrent scheduling and assertion protection. Completed empty and skipped suites retain their existing behavior. This is a guard against premature termination, not hostile test code forging the token.

Validation: all eight focused end-to-end tests pass under `-I -O -B` on Windows/Python 3.12.14 and 3.14.5 with workspace TEMP/TMP. Controls include discovery-time `SystemExit(0)`, execution-time `os._exit(0)`, exact child argv, valid empty/skipped suites, ordinary failures, concurrency and optimized-parent assertion coverage. The actual before/after witness changes from false PASS/exit0 to identified incomplete module/exit1. No full selected-frontier replay or speed claim.

Started from canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4; the prescribed baseline binding check passed. The documentation records the changed verifier-engineering scope and credits the inherited isolated scheduler and assertion guard. No frozen inputs or selected frontier change. Prepared by ywz65 with OpenAI Codex assistance.
